The announcement was made by the Secretary of the Treasury on June 16 that holders of the Treasury 1-1/8 percent certificates of indebtedness, Series F-1949, maturing July 1, 1949, would be offered in exchange a new one-year 1-1/4 percent certificate of indebtedness. The maturing certificates totaled $5,783 million.

Subscription books for the exchange offering were opened June 20 and were closed at the close of business on June 23. The new certificates, Series F-1950, were dated July 1, 1949, and bear interest from that date at the rate of 1-1/4 per-cent per annum, payable with the principal at maturity on July 1, 1950. Exchanges were made par for par and cash subscriptions were not received. The certificates were issued in bearer form only, in denominations of $1,000, $5,000, $10,000, $100,000, and $1,000,000.
Note: Details of Treasury market financing operations are shown in the tables on "Offerings" and "Disposition", respectively, of marketable issues of bonds, notes,

Reports to the Treasury on the ownership of Government securities indicate that on April 30, 1949, about 65 percent of the maturing certificates were owned by reporting commercial banks and Federal Reserve Banks. The ownership figures for April 30 are the latest available for holdings of commercial banks.
Subscriptions to the new certificates of indebtedness totaled $5,601 million on the basis of preliminary figures, leaving $182 million of the maturing issue to be paid in cash.

Treasury bills maturing in June were refunded in the full amount of $4.5 billion. Each issue amounted to $900 million. The average rate of discount on the issue dated June 2 was 1.159 percent, and on the other four issues the average rate was 1.158 percent.

Information relating to capital movements between the United States and foreign countries is presented in four sections. Section II supplies a geographic breakdown by principal countries for recent months. The total net capital movement is given first and then the principal categories are shown separately. Section III presents details with respect to capital movements and short-term claims and liabilities. These are shown for the latest month for which final data are

Section IV contains data for recent months on outstanding contracts of banks for forward purchases and sales of foreign exchange.

The data in these four sections are based on reports filled each month by banks, bankers, and brokers throughout the United States. The reports are collected, checked, and tabulated by the twelve Federal Reserve Banks. The totals are then forwarded to the Treasury Department for consolidation and publication.
